title: Portal resellers
description: Reseller organisations and their commercial terms (portal plan P6.1; D2189, D2190, D2191). A reseller is an organisation that sells to its own customers: it creates their organisations and invites their first owners, it is never a member of them (F40), it sees their keys' metadata and never a key (F5), and what it owes Fugaro accrues daily against a credit limit operations set. Every object here is closed, because ee/keyservice/wire_resellers.go decodes it with DisallowUnknownFields.

reseller.description: One reseller organisation's commercial terms, as the reseller reads them and as operations sets them (P6.1's TestCreditLimitAndRatesAreOperationsSet).

organisation_id.description: The reseller organisation itself. Only operations creates one (D2191), and its type is what makes the sign-in rule apply to its members (F10).

credit_limit_micros.description: The ceiling on unpaid accrual, in micro-dollars (D2189). It is a limit and not a balance: nothing is prepaid, and a mint that would pass it is refused rather than queued. Zero is a reseller that may not mint at all, which is not the same as one nobody set a limit for.

rates.description: One wholesale price per policy row. A row with no rate here is a row this reseller cannot sell: a missing price is not a price of zero.

created_at.description: When the reseller organisation was created, in UTC.

rate.description: One row's wholesale price for one reseller.

row.description: The policy row this price is for, by name, as a mint names one.

daily_rate_micros.description: What one seat of that row costs the reseller a day, in micro-dollars. Daily is the unit because accrual is days times seats times this (D2189), and it has to stop the day an entitlement is revoked rather than at the end of a term that was never served.

customer.description: One customer organisation a reseller sold to, as the reseller's own list answers it.

organisation_id.description: The customer organisation. Its own owners are its owners: the reseller is not a member of it (F40).

name.description: The customer organisation's name, which is what the reseller's list shows.

reseller_organisation_id.description: The link, carried here and not only on the customer because operations can relink one (P6.1): a customer whose reseller changed is a customer whose accrual moves with it, and a list read months later has to say which reseller it belonged to then.

linked_at.description: When the link was made, in UTC. A relink writes a new one rather than editing this.

relink.description: Operations' request to move one customer organisation from one reseller to another (P6.1). It is audited, and it does not move money: the ledger's lines carry the channel they had when they were written (see ledger.schema.json).

reseller_organisation_id.description: The reseller organisation it is being relinked to. Only operations sets this link (D2191): a reseller that could claim a customer could claim its accrual.
